body:
## Summary

`ec_aipw()` matches each outcome formula to an outcome by position in the list. It does not use the left side of the formula to match. If the order of `outcome_formula` is different from the order of `outcome_col_name`, the result is incorrect. The function gives no message.

## Steps to reproduce

```r
library(rdborrow)
f1 <- "y1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5"
f2 <- "y2 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5"

fit <- function(outcome_formula) {
  method <- ec_aipw("S ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5", outcome_formula)
  analysis <- setup_analysis_primary(
    data = SyntheticData,
    trial_status_col_name = "S",
    treatment_col_name = "A",
    outcome_col_name = c("y1", "y2"),
    covariates_col_name = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5"),
    method_weighting_obj = method
  )
  run_analysis(analysis)$results$point_estimates
}

fit(c(f1, f2))
fit(c(f2, f1))
```

## Expected result

Both calls give the same estimates. Alternatively, the second call stops with an error that identifies the mismatch.

## Actual result

```
fit(c(f1, f2))  #> -0.546  0.540
fit(c(f2, f1))  #> -0.127  0.121
```

The standard errors are also different.

## Cause

`.ec_aipw_core()` fits each formula with `lm()`, so the left side of formula t sets the fitted outcome. Then the code subtracts prediction t from outcome t (`R/ec_aipw.R:206-212`). If the two orders are different, the code subtracts a prediction for `y2` from `y1`.

## Correction

1. Match each formula to an outcome by the left side of the formula.
2. Stop with an error if a left side is not one of the outcomes.
3. Stop with an error if an outcome has no formula, or has more than one formula.

Add a test that gives the formulas in a different order and gets the same estimates.

## Affected functions

| Function | Location |
|---|---|
| `ec_aipw()` | `R/ec_aipw.R:206-212` |
| `did_ec_aipw()`, `did_ec_or()` | Possibly the same pattern. Not yet examined. |

## Related

Found by three testers in the adversarial review pilot (#101).
title: ec_aipw() matches outcome formulas to outcomes by position
